properties.statement: A LANE WHOSE DELIVERABLE WAS A DENOMINATOR HAD TO HAND-DERIVE IT TWICE, BECAUSE THE READ SURFACE CANNOT ANSWER A SET QUESTION. Reported 2026-08-08 by w-4d05e937 (dev_storyflow, LANE UNSUSPECTED-VALIDATION-WALK), items 1 and 3. TWO INDEPENDENT MISSES, ONE SHAPE. (1) `get_node` RETURNS PROPERTIES BUT NO EDGES. Their brief required excluding capabilities that already carry a walk-type Verification — a VERIFIES edge query. get_node on a Verification returns kind/status/method/level/name and nothing about what it verifies; evidence_report gives per-capability check COUNTS but never WHICH check. The only routes they could see to the actual edges were a full unscoped detect_gaps dump or an export, which workers are told not to take. THEY FELL BACK TO MATCHING VERIFICATION NAMES AGAINST CAPABILITY IDS AND HAD TO PUBLISH THAT AS A STATED WEAKNESS IN THEIR OWN METHOD. (2) `scan_nodes` HAS NO STATUS FILTER. Their population was 'every Capability with status realized or verified'; they pulled all 95 and tallied by hand. It happened to agree with the boss's independent count — and their own comment is the right one: HAND-TALLYING IS EXACTLY WHERE A DENOMINATOR QUIETLY DRIFTS, AND THE DENOMINATOR WAS THE DELIVERABLE. NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH cap:bounded-reads, which is working correctly and makes this worse: scan_nodes honestly reports `omitted` and `capped_by` when a payload fills, so a hand-tally over a large type is not merely tedious, it is a paging loop the reader must get right. FIX SHAPE, theirs: `get_node(..., with_edges: true)`, or a `verifies_report` mirroring evidence_report but NAMING the target; and `scan_nodes(node_type, status: [...])` or a `count_by_status`. Both are cheap, and both turn a guessable answer into a checkable one.
